subject: Draft: first-output SLO and adaptive chunk rhythm
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Desai <amina@datagrid.com>
Cc: Rory Holt <rory.holt@datagrid.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: first-output SLO and adaptive chunk rhythm

Hi Amina / Rory —

Thanks again for the deep-dive today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps for the engineering readout: 

Summary of customer goals (as discussed)
- Primary SLO: time-to-first-token (first-output) at p95 <= 120ms for the initial prompt path (text completion for short prompts ~32 tokens).
- Target sustained throughput: 450 qps at peak region (US-East), with peak concurrency bursts up to 800 concurrent requests for short windows.
- Streaming requirements: user experience must be low-latency incremental chunks for UI streaming. You prefer SSE where supported, fall back to WebSocket for older clients.
- Chunk cadence: target 200–500ms between chunks for typical model outputs, with ability to reduce to 100ms for interactive flows.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Default delivery: SSE with adaptive chunk cadence (server-driven pacing that targets perceptible increments while honoring latency SLO).
- TTFT guarantee path: aim to meet p95 120ms on our Dedicated offering with pre-warmed KV cache and short-sequence kernel. If you need hosted credits to pilot, we can open a sandbox with reserved concurrency.
- Overload/fallbacks: automatic model fallback to a smaller quantized variant for degraded periods (keeps UX streaming but shorter chunks).

Open clarifying questions (ask the ENG/product folks to confirm):
1) Can you confirm the distribution of prompt lengths? (mostly 16–64 tokens, or do you have a fat tail?)
2) Are there strict cookie-cutter clients where WebSocket is required and SSE cannot be used?
3) Any regulatory need to keep traffic in a specific region or VPC?

Next steps
- Amina to confirm prompt-length distribution and call out any non-SSE clients (Rory/Amina).
- Redwood to share a condensed performance matrix (attached) with suggested instance profiles, expected p95 TTFT ranges, and chunk cadence options (Ben/Marissa).
- Schedule a 30-min engineering sync next week to land on final SLO and a pilot window.

Attachments: datagrid_requirements.xlsx (your sheet), perf-matrix.csv (Redwood suggested configs)

Thanks — will wait for your confirmations and will propose times for the sync.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: perf-matrix.csv contains rough p95 estimates for each hardware tier and model variant; numbers assume prefix caching enabled and 32-token prompts.

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: first-output SLO and adaptive chunk rhythm

Thanks Priya — this is helpful and aligns with our internal notes. Quick answers inline: 

- Prompt distribution: ~70% of requests are 8–24 tokens, 25% are 25–80 tokens, and roughly 5% are longer (200+ tokens) during batch summarization windows.
- Clients: Web app and mobile both support EventSource (SSE) in our modern SDK; however we have an enterprise on-prem agent that only supports WebSocket and TLS-over-proxy so WebSocket fallback is required.
- Data locality: must remain in US-East for this pilot due to data residency policies.

The TTFT p95 <= 120ms goal is aggressive but a good target for the interactive flows (the 8–24 token path). For the longer tail we expect higher latency; plan is to use smaller quantized variants for those requests or async batch.

Can Ben/Marissa confirm the perf-matrix assumptions you mentioned (particularly cache hit rate and warm workers per shard)? If you can, also add an estimate of the minimum steady-state reserved concurrency we should commit to for the pilot (we can commit to a 3-month pilot if the numbers look reasonable).

Happy to join a 30-min eng sync next week — Tues/Wed preferred.

Regards,
Amina
Director of Product Engineering, DataGrid
amina@datagrid.com

Hi Amina —

Thanks for the quick clarifications, that distribution helps a lot. A couple of concrete answers to your asks (summarized from perf-matrix assumptions):

Assumptions baked into perf-matrix.csv (attached)
- Cache hit rate: modeled at 65% prefix hit for interactive flows (we can run probes to validate; if you have cached prompts that improves numbers).
- Warm workers per shard: baseline config uses 16 warm workers per shard for the small- to medium-sized models; larger models use 32.
- Kernel/seq assumptions: p95 TTFT numbers assume 32-token effective input for the interactive path.

Suggested reserved concurrency for pilot
- For a target of 450 qps sustained with 800 burst concurrency, we recommend reserving at least 400 concurrent slots on Dedicated for the pilot to guarantee isolation and predictable p95 behavior (300 baseline with 100 burst buffer). We can provide an initial pricing sketch if you confirm pilot duration.

Chunk cadence behavior and fallback
- Adaptive cadence: our runtime will pace chunks by default to the 200–400ms band for generated tokens when the model length is short; for interactive flows where you want more granular realtime feel we can push to ~100ms but that increases token overhead and cost slightly.
- WebSocket vs SSE: we will default to SSE and maintain a WebSocket endpoint for your on-prem agent. Both endpoints will honor the same pacing policy server-side.
- Fallback model: we can configure an automatic fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant when node pressure is high; this preserves chunking behavior while reducing inference latency/cost.

Next steps (actionable)
- Priya: schedule 30-min engineering sync (Tues/Wed).
- Amina: confirm pilot commitment window and whether DataGrid signs an NDA/PO before pilot.
- Ben/Marissa: we'll upload a slightly expanded perf-matrix with a reserve-concurrency column and a conservative cost estimate for the 3-month pilot.

Attaching perf-matrix.csv now (CSV stub).

—Ben
